**Visual Analysis:**

**Affected plant parts:** Stems (longitudinal cross-sections) and root system of what appears to be a solanaceous plant (likely tomato).

**Key visual features:**
- Two stems shown side-by-side in a longitudinal view, revealing **internal vascular tissue**
- Extensive **brown to tan discoloration running through the vascular (xylem) tissue** of both stems — the brown streaking follows the vascular bundles along the length of the stem
- The outer cortex also shows brown/necrotic banding
- The **root system is extensively rotted** — roots appear brown, deteriorated, and fibrous
- No white mycelium, sclerotia, water-soaking, or powdery growth visible
- The discoloration is internal/systemic rather than surface lesions

**Reasoning through differential diagnosis:**
- **Southern Blight**: Requires white cottony mycelium and sclerotia at soil line — absent here
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot**: Needs cottony white growth and sclerotia inside stem — not visible
- **Bacterial Wilt/Southern Bacterial Wilt**: Can cause vascular browning but typically shows bacterial ooze
- **Rhizopus Soft Rots**: Soft, mushy tissue with dark sporangia — not present
- **Verticillium Wilt**: Classic hallmark is **internal brown-to-tan vascular discoloration** visible in stem cross-sections/longitudinal cuts, combined with root deterioration — this matches exactly what is shown here

The brown vascular streaking (discolored xylem) running lengthwise through the stem, combined with root system collapse, is the textbook presentation of **Verticillium Wilt**.
